# Ls014 — Untyped (`*`) attribute used where derived not declared / `$` confused with `*`

## Sources
- T024, Q087, N022, N046

## Description

`*` denotes derived/inherited attribute; `$` denotes null OPTIONAL value. Generators substitute one for the other. Inside aggregate elements only `$` is permitted as a "no value" placeholder; `*` is an attribute-level marker only. Some senders also emit a value for a derived slot instead of `*`.

## Reproducer recipe

`#1=SI_ENERGY_UNIT((#2),*,$,.JOULE.);` vs `#1=SI_ENERGY_UNIT((#2),$,$,.JOULE.);`; `#1=POLYLINE('',(*,#10,#11));` (`*` inside list).

## Expected kernel behavior

Schema-aware kernel cross-checks `*`/`$` against the attribute kind in EXPRESS; reject `*` inside list elements; emit "expected `*` (derived)" rather than a generic type error.

**Structured outcomes** (extracted from prose; for downstream auto-grading):
- allowed: `reject`
